messages.author: 54c05e928c45ac6c
messages.subject: Re: Bifactor modelling
parts:
1. You're treating all of your endogenous variables as ordered with "ordered == TRUE" which estimates many thresholds. In total, you're estimating 73 parameters with 171 observations.  When you're asking this much of such little data, you can have issues with convergence. The issues may (not) be flagged by warnings/errors based on optimizer parameters and the shape of the likelihood. Recommend starting with a simpler model if there are issues (without ordered = TRUE).
2. I'm not sure why you are concerned about negative covariances. Covariance can be positive or negative.
3. Unless you have a theoretical reason to do otherwise, you probably want to free the first loading for each factor.
4. Advise against using modification indices given the size of your model and data unless you really want to overfit and get unstable, non-robust results - even if this is exploratory work.

Hi Brett, thank you so so much for your response. 

My understanding based on the advice here: https://groups.google.com/g/lavaan/c/tnTZwMzN0lw was that setting ordered=TRUE was preferrable for ordinal data on a likert scale, which I am attempting to estimate. This bifactor model is exploratory however and negative loadings may be due to the sample size. 

I flagged the negative covariance as it is conceptually unusual for my scale, though still plausible, so wanted to rule out any model misspecification. Unfortunately fixing negative loadings to zero after removing the ordered = TRUE command resulted in non-converfence so I suspect sample size is the issue here.

On Tuesday, May 24, 2022 at 11:17:35 AM UTC-7 aku...@gmail.com wrote:
Hi all,

I am trying to conduct a bifactor model on a likert scale with 176 participants (171 complete cases). 

I have specified a bifactor model with the general factor as orthogonal to the group factor as below but allowed the group factors to be non-orthogonal as otherwise I get negative variance estimates. 


model.bi1 <- 'IU =~ iu1 + iu2 + iu3 + iu4 + iu5 + iu6 + iu7 + iu8 + iu9 + iu10 + iu11 + iu12
              PA =~ iu1 + iu2 + iu4 + iu5 + iu8 + iu9 + iu11
              IA =~ iu3 + iu6 + iu7 + iu10 + iu12
             
              # Orthogonality
              IU ~~ 0*PA
              IU ~~ 0*IA
             
              # variances to one
              PA ~~ 1*PA
              IA ~~ 1*IA
              IU ~~ 1*IU
              '

I have run a cfa using lavaan as below, using the estimator recommended for ordinal data and removing data listwise (otherwise the estimator does not run)

model.bi.fit1 <- lavaan::cfa(model.bi1, data=iucombined,
                            std.lv = TRUE, ordered = TRUE,
                            estimator = "WLSMV", missing = "listwise")


lavaan converged after this, however I have a negative covariance between PA and IA and some negative lambdas (see output below). Removing the cases or working with modification indices didn't produce an admissible solution. Given that lavaan converged and that the standard errors look reasonable I wanted to ask the google group if this output is trustworthy to interpret? I am skeptical of the negative lambdas but am not sure how to move forward as they are very small estimates in general. I've tried fixing the negative lambdas to zero, but this still results in a negative covariance between PA and IA.

Any help or guidance is greatly appreciated!
